learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of slicing, sharing, and scaling numbers to solve real-world food, money, and distance puzzles!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Multiplying fractions is just finding a part of a part. If you have half a cake (1/2) and you eat half of that piece (1/2), you actually ate one-fourth (1/4) of the whole cake!
Dividing fractions can sound scary, but it has a simple trick. You just flip the second fraction upside down (making it a reciprocal) and change the division sign to multiplication. Easy!
We use fraction multiplication to scale things up or down. If a recipe for 4 people needs 2/3 cups of sugar, multiplying the fraction helps us find out how much we need for 8 people.

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Digroz Learning Recipe Scaler
fun_activity.instructions: Find a recipe in your kitchen that uses fractions (like 1/2 cup of flour). Rewrite the ingredients list to show exactly how much you would need if you were cooking for twice as many people!

quick_recap: ⭐ Multiplying fractions means multiplying the top numbers together and the bottom numbers together.
⭐ To divide fractions, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second.
⭐ Fractions are essential for scaling recipes, maps, and building plans.
